newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine union boss calls for higher mininum wage.
newsitem.headline: Argentine union boss calls for higher mininum wage.

text.p: The head of Argentina's CGT trades union confederation Thursday called for a rise in the mininum wage and pensions.
At the end of a union meeting, Rodolfo Daer called for an "urgent substantial improvement in the minimum wage and a rise in retirement pay and pensions", local media reported.

Asked by local television whether the CGT could call another strike to follow up the 36-hour stoppage in September and a 24-hour strike in August, Daer said: "One does not rule out a day of protest, which could be a strike or a march."
Unions have said they may stage a 48-hour general strike against government plans to introduce more flexible labor rules, but have recently let the threat quietly drop.
But the once close ties between the unions and President Carlos Menem are still strained.
